GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2013-03-08T14:40:31Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: delegating events on inherited views
Description: I have a BaseView which defines some events delegation specifying an events hash.

Then I have a CustomView (extending BaseView) that also defines their own events, by also specifying an event hash.

If I'm not wrong, BaseView's event hash is overwritten, so theirs events are not processed by delegateEvent.

The documentation says to use an events function instead of a hash to handle this case.

I solved it with something like this:

on the parent's render method I mix the parent's events with those from the child

``` javascript
    this.delegateEvents(_.merge(this.events, {
      'show .accordion': 'collapsePanelGroup',
      'hide .accordion': 'collapsePanelGroup'
    }));
```

I guess this could be a pretty common scenario, so I was wondering if it's worth the effort to add something like this to delegateEvents:

``` javascript
delegateEvents: function(events, preserve) {
```

Passing a preserve = true, would just add this.events to events and then process, or maybe define some addEvent method

What would be the most appropriate to hadle this scenario?
